rv.q: The Ladies Football Club is most stirring when it challenges that idea, drawing a line from the spirit and defiance of these women more than a century ago to the triumphs of their Lionesses successors today.
It’s difficult to say why a production that ended in a wildly enthusiastic standing ovation left me comparatively underwhelmed.
But the overall effect is of playing with a half-inflated ball: you can kick it as hard as you want – it ain't gonna fly.
It's impossible not to be moved by this production; it's an extraordinary piece of theatre.
The performances are authentic and passionate, and at times, genuinely moving.
The Ladies Football Club is a joyous production, combining witty dialogue with energetic movement.

cn.t: Critics praise this spirited account of women's football origins during WWI, highlighting its humor, dynamic ensemble work, and excellent choreographed movement sequences that bring the pioneering players' story to energetic life.
